name: RunRecapTab

states.name: Run Outcome at a Glance
states.description: When a user navigates to the Summary page after a workflow completes, they need to immediately understand the outcome. The page should communicate whether the run succeeded, failed, or was stopped, along with the AI-generated narrative of what was accomplished. This is the most critical information on the page because it determines whether the user needs to take further action or can move on to another task.

states.name: Failure Analysis and Recovery
states.description: When a workflow run fails, users need to understand what went wrong and have options for recovery. The Summary page should prominently display failure details for failed runs and offer a way to continue the run with additional iterations. This is essential for iterative development workflows where partial progress is common and users want to pick up where they left off rather than starting over.

states.name: Tabbed Deep-Dive Sections
states.description: Beyond the top-level summary, users need to drill into specific aspects of the run. The tabbed interface provides organized access to the execution timeline, verification results, knowledge entries, context variables, canvas artifacts, and error monitoring. Each tab serves a distinct analytical purpose, and users should be able to switch between them fluidly to build a complete picture of what happened.

states.name: Phase Timeline Tab — Content & Structure

requiredElements.text: No phase results yet for this run

states.description: When the Phase Timeline tab is active, the user sees one collapsible card per PhaseResult row. Each card shows the phase name (Setup / Verification / Agentic / Completion), optional iteration number, optional stage index, a success/failure badge, the phase duration, step count (successful/total), and an optional abbreviated 8-char commit hash. Iteration separators appear between cards whenever the iteration field changes, so multi-iteration runs read chronologically. The tab is backed by the get_phase_results Tauri command reading from the runner.phase_results PG table (plan: restate-port-part-a-compensation-and-phase-results.md §2.5).
states.precondition: Phase Timeline tab is active and at least one phase_result row exists for the selected run

states.name: Phase Timeline — PhaseResult Data Correctness
states.description: The Phase Timeline is a window into the loop controller's structured PhaseResult output. The controller builds one PhaseResult after each phase executor returns (setup, verification, agentic, completion) at four insertion points in loop_controller.rs and loop_handlers.rs, persists it via save_phase_result, and emits it on the Tauri 'phase-result' event. Persistence and emit both key on get_parent_task_id(&config.execution_id) so composed-run children surface under their parent task_run. Correctness assertions describe what the persisted data must look like on the page — deviations indicate bugs in the loop controller's mapping logic, not the UI.
states.precondition: Phase Timeline tab is active with at least one card

states.name: Empty and Loading States
states.description: The Summary page must gracefully handle states where data is not yet available. When a run is loading, the user should see clear progress indication. When no run is selected or no recap data exists, the page should guide the user toward selecting a run or initiating one. These states prevent confusion and ensure the user always knows what to do next.

states.name: Verification Results Pagination
states.description: The Verification tab paginates iteration results (20 per page) to handle runs with many verification iterations. The latest visible iteration is auto-expanded. A 'Show more' button loads additional iterations.
states.precondition: A task run with >20 verification iterations is selected and Verification tab is active

description: Run Summary page — the primary post-run analysis view where users understand what happened during a workflow run. Combines AI-generated summaries, status banners, token usage, failure details, and tabbed deep-dive sections (Timeline, Verification, Knowledge, Context, Canvas, Diffs & Replay, Phase Timeline, Feedback Scores, LLM Costs, Errors).
